mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of quarters where this trigger occurs, or the effect reverses in a low-inflation environment.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during periods of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of such episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of high wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, which compresses real earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such stagflation triggers, or the effect reverses when commodity prices surge.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals robust domestic demand, which boosts earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of such episodes, or the effect is nullified during periods of high external trade deficits.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the prior 12-month average for three consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of wage stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in both industrial production (INDPRO) and the producer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their 3-month averages indicates an inflationary supply expansion, which initially boosts earnings but later erodes margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days but negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of such episodes, or the short-term positive effect fails to materialize during energy price spikes.
